context: seed: what a mature store for the reasoning-core stream holds — no observation behind it; the fork is read off the family's prompt (suite/families/reasoning_core.py:66, suite/families/reasoning_core.py:76), its budgets (suite/families/reasoning_core.py:47, suite/families/reasoning_core.py:50) and the checkers (suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:58, suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:73); the lax pool budgets the knowing call plus one, the strict pool exactly the knowing call, and the tool layer counts before it refuses
counterfactual: The overshoot is the third call: the probe of this stream saw a pass under the budget of two (suite/families/reasoning_core.py:47, suite/families/reasoning_core.py:59) make a third shell call on a regex instance, refused with `call budget of 2 exceeded at call 3` (suite/tools.py:87) and counted (suite/tools.py:84), so the row failed tool_budget_respected while the task itself had been solvable in one. The other overshoot is a first call that proves nothing — `python3 -c 'import nltk'` — which under the strict budget (suite/families/reasoning_core.py:47) leaves no call for the verification the method rests on.
decision: Treat the shell budget as exactly what the prompt states: every call counts — one refused past the budget and one that exits nonzero count too — and the budget is met when the verification is the first call. Spend no call finding out whether python3, `re` or `nltk` exist (they do), printing or echoing the pattern or grammar, listing files, or splitting one verification across calls; derive the candidate in reasoning and make the verifying call the first one, with the whole check in that one command (a heredoc is one call). Make the command exit 0 whatever the verdict — print True or False, never let an exception escape — so the one call always returns a verdict. If the verdict is False: under a budget of 1 do not call again — re-derive from the structure and return the re-derived candidate; under a budget of 2 the second call verifies one re-derived candidate and there is no third. Never make a call you expect to be refused: it is counted all the same.

residue: whether the re-derived candidate under a budget of one was right is judgment; the floor checks the call count against the budget

options.name: A — the verifying call is the first call; no probing, no printing, no splitting; under a budget of one a False verdict is repaired by re-derivation, not by a second call
options.why: the tool layer increments the counter before checking the budget (suite/tools.py:84, suite/tools.py:87), so an over-budget call is both refused and counted; python3 with re and nltk is on the PATH, so nothing needs probing

options.name: B — spend a first call checking the environment, then verify
options.why: the environment is known; the check costs the strict pool its only call and the lax pool its repair

options.name: C — when the verdict is False under a budget of one, verify the repaired candidate anyway
options.why: the call is refused, counted, and fails tool_budget_respected for a verdict it never delivers
